messages:
sophie: FYI customer reported a sudden p99 jump for /v1/generate around 14:12 UTC — looks like our dashboard shows a much bigger spike than the raw histogram panel :grimacing:
opsbot: Alert: service/api-gateway p99 > 1200ms at 2026-03-17T14:12:06Z (alert-id: alert-1192)
sophie: Linking screenshots: https://img.company/reports/2890012345/heatmap.png and dashboard panel: https://grafana.company/d/svc-latency?panelId=8
mina: Can you paste the raw query for the histogram panel? Are we comparing a rollup-based quantile vs raw-event quantile?
jordan: I pulled both panels — dashboard A (rollup) uses a 1m rollup window with `quantile(0.99, rate(latency_sum[5m]) / rate(latency_count[5m]))` style calc; histogram panel B is derived from ingest histograms and uses fixed buckets -> we might be mixing two different derivations.
sophie: exactly — customer-facing SLA checks the histogram-based p99, but our support dashboard default is rollup-derived. Need to confirm which one we promised in the incident email.
kai: Quick repro hypothesis: if the ingest agent rebinned buckets at 14:10 (we had that batching flag flip), the histogram panel will show a discontinuity while rollup smoothing may under/overestimate quantiles. Check deploy-bot.
opsbot: Deploy: infra/deploy-batcher v2.3.1 -> production at 2026-03-17T14:09:58Z by @ramon (change: enable_auto_rebin true)
ramon: That was my change — enabled auto_rebin for memory savings. I didn't expect p99 to move that much. Will roll back if it's the cause.
mina: Before rollback, can we validate with a direct query against raw events? Use this snippet: `SELECT quantile(0.99, latency_ms) FROM api_latency WHERE ts >= now() - 15m GROUP BY histogram_bucket(0,10,20,50,100,250,500,1000,2000)` (adapted to our metrics store).
jordan: I ran a quick diff: raw-event quantile (15m) = 520ms; rollup-derived panel = 1180ms; ingest-histogram panel = 490ms. Rollup is the outlier.
sophie: So rollup math is inflating p99 during bursts. Is it because the rollup uses max-window or samples across minute boundaries?
kai: It looks like rollup pipeline uses a weighted-mean approach but then applies `quantile()` on aggregated buckets, which is biased for heavy tails. Also our rollup window was changed from 1m->5m in the last infra config push (maybe unintentional). Check config: `/etc/rollup/rollup.conf` shows `window_seconds = 300` on prod.
ramon: Ugh — that was part of the batching change to reduce write ops. I can flip window_seconds back to 60 as a hotfix.
mina: Hotfix plan: (1) rollup-window -> 60s rollback (ramon), (2) set dashboard panels to show derivation source clearly (jordan), (3) post a note to support explaining metric sources (sophie). Also open a ticket to evaluate stable quantile algorithm for rollups.
jordan: Quick dashboard patch: change panel title to include "(rollup-derived)" and add a small notice: "For SLA use raw-event quantiles". I'll push that to Grafana now.
sophie: Customer update: "We identified a metrics derivation mismatch introduced by a recent rollup config change; application latency did not increase to the degree shown on some dashboards. We're rolling back the rollup window and will follow up with full postmortem." Want me to send?
mina: Send it and include the raw numbers + timeline. I'll attach the diff screenshot.
ramon: Rolling back now. ETA ~3m.
opsbot: Action: rollback job started for infra/deploy-batcher (rollback to v2.3.0) at 2026-03-17T14:21:10Z
ramon: Rolled back, rollup window back to 60s. Watching metrics.
jordan: After rollback: rollup-derived p99 aligns with ingest histogram (~500ms). Heatmap spike resolved.
sophie: Great. For follow-ups: ticket to research stable rollup quantile algorithm, doc to standardize "which metric to quote" in customer comms, and a flag guard on auto_rebin changes (requires owner + SRE signoff).
mina: I'll create the ticket and assign to eng-metrics. Ticket# METRICS-4821
ramon: Sorry everyone — my bad on the config change. Will add a canary for any future auto_rebin flips.
sophie: No worries, thanks for the quick rollback. Closing for now — I'll post a short incident summary in #postmortems later. :thumbsup:
